replies.text:
Hi Sanjog (or Sanjog's agent),

Please find the answers to Q1–Q6 below.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Q1 – FACE WASH ON BLINKIT: WHAT'S DRIVING THE GAP?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The gap is driven by Detan Ubtan Face Wash.

• Ubtan sold 2,939 units in Oct 22–27 vs 3,530 at September pro-rata: down
591 units (−17%).
• Anti Acne Neem Face Wash grew from 141 to 275 units (+134), but this
recovers less than a quarter of the Ubtan loss.

Seven cities account for half of the Ubtan drop (−302 of −591 units):

• Mumbai: 331 → 247 (−84) | OSA 83% → 90%
• Delhi: 479 → 416 (−63) | OSA 89% → 97%
• Jaipur: 100 → 59 (−41) | OSA 81% → 98%
• Hyderabad: 90 → 51 (−39) | OSA 87% → 81%
• Ludhiana: 45 → 17 (−28) | OSA 79% → 89%
• Ghaziabad: 218 → 193 (−25) | OSA 86% → 98%
• Lucknow: 88 → 66 (−22) | OSA 81% → 91%
(Units: Sep pro-rata → Oct 22–27)

Availability is not the issue. OSA in these cities was 89–98% and improved
vs September in six of the seven; national Ubtan OSA rose from 76% to 89%.
Hyderabad is the only exception (OSA slipped to 81%).

The driver is lower branded search (keyword tracker, L30D, 27 Sep vs 27
Oct):
• "nat habit face wash": ~37,500 → ~24,600 (−34%)
• "nat habit ubtan face wash": ~1,760 → ~1,040 (−41%)

Fewer brand searches led to fewer Ubtan orders despite strong availability.
The target was set on the assumption that branded searches would grow by at
least 20%.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Q2 – LOOFAH ON BLINKIT: WHAT'S DRIVING THE GAP?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The gap is both vs target and vs last month, and availability is the driver.

The target above last month assumed we would increase ad SOV to grow market
share. Because availability dropped across major cities, we could not scale
up spends, and units fell overall.

• Loofah sold 1,276 units in Oct 22–27 vs 1,469 at September pro-rata: down
193 units (−13%).
• National OSA fell from 85% to 83%, but the drop is concentrated in key
cities:

• Delhi: 93 → 57 (−36) | OSA 92% → 52%
• Ghaziabad: 40 → 17 (−23) | OSA 88% → 68%
• Pune: 66 → 50 (−16) | OSA 90% → 74%
• Jaipur: 25 → 12 (−13) | OSA 95% → 88%
• Lucknow: 21 → 14 (−7) | OSA 89% → 76%
• Ranchi: 14 → 8 (−6) | OSA 97% → 85%
(Units: Sep pro-rata → Oct 22–27)

These six cities make up −101 units, more than half the drop, and every one
of them lost availability.

We have stock in the backend, but movement to the frontend (dark stores) is
slow due to space constraints. We are actively following up, but expect
this to be resolved only after Diwali.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Q3 – FACE WASH ON ZEPTO: WHAT'S DRIVING THE GAP?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

On Zepto, face wash is a single SKU: Brightening Ubtan Face Wash.

• Sold 612 units in Oct 22–28 vs 733 at September pro-rata: down 121 units
(−17%).
• The +3.9% WoW (588 → 612 units) is a small recovery that has not closed
the gap to September levels.

Six cities account for almost the entire gap (−119 of −121 units):

• Delhi: 125 → 72 (−53)
• Mumbai: 168 → 152 (−16)
• Noida: 44 → 30 (−14)
• Bengaluru: 79 → 66 (−13)
• Jaipur: 28 → 15 (−13)
• Lucknow: 26 → 16 (−10)
(Units: Sep pro-rata → Oct 22–28)

Pune (+9), Kolkata (+9) and Faridabad (+6) grew, but not enough to offset
these.

Two factors drove the gap:

1. Branded search fell instead of growing. "nat habit face wash" averaged
~270 searches/day in September vs ~158/day in Oct 22–28 (−42%). Overall
brand search ("nat habit") was roughly flat (~1,025 → ~985/day), so the
decline is specific to face wash. The target assumed branded searches would
rise.

2. The availability improvement was delayed. The target assumed face wash
would move from super store to dark store this month, lifting availability
from ~80% to at least 90%. Due to the festive period, this move was
postponed and has only just happened. We expect the availability impact to
show from next month.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Q4 – SOAP ON ZEPTO: IS THE SPEND EARNING ITS KEEP?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Yes, and this is not the right time to pull it back.

• Soap has almost no organic visibility on Zepto: organic share of search
is 0.04% vs 4.67% from ads.
• This is why ads make up 95.6% of soap sales, vs 29.3% for Zepto overall.
If we stop spending, visibility drops to near zero and sales go with it.

Zepto's algorithm rewards DRR: SKUs that sell consistently every day rank
higher in organic search. Soap's DRR is currently too low to earn organic
ranking, which is why organic SoV is so small. Ad spend is what builds that
DRR, and at ROAS 1.16 (vs 1.21 last week) it is paying for itself while
doing so.

Plan: keep spending now to build DRR, then taper. As DRR and conversion
improve, organic units will take over and ad spend can come down step by
step. We will start reducing once organic share of search and the organic
share of soap sales begin climbing week on week.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Q5 – LEPA ON ZEPTO: IS THE SPEND EARNING ITS KEEP?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Yes. The higher spend was a deliberate move to cover lost organic units,
and it has paid off.

Why organic fell short: the plan assumed Lepa's organic units would rise
over the festive season. As a fresh product, Lepa's availability was not
pushed by Zepto and is currently averaging only ~55%, so organic sales fell
well short of plan.

What we did: we raised ad spend to ₹83,869 (137% of the ad plan) to make up
for those lost organic units. It worked:
• ROAS improved from 1.13 to 1.31 WoW.
• Cost per order came in lower than last month and lower than target.

Ads at 142% of sales reflects this: with organic units this weak, nearly
every Lepa order is coming through ads. The figure is above 100% because
Zepto credits ads with sales beyond the SKU's direct sales, such as
indirect orders.

Should we pull it back? Not yet. Lepa is planned to move to dark stores
after Diwali, which should lift availability and bring organic units back.
Once organic sales recover, we will bring ad spend back toward plan.


━━━━━━━━━━━━
